clue.text: Go without English beer

indicators.note: without means the next piece is left out of the phrase for going

parts.note: to go on a journey is to set out

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave, going without a pint of English beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' seems to be an instruction, but it is SET OUT; dropping its E leaves the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout is a dark, strong kind of beer brewed with roasted malt.

clue.text: Chap, informally, has knocked back gin and collapsed

parts.note: a chap is casually called a fella

indicators.note: knocked back means the word for the snare is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: A bloke downs a gin and keels over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink being knocked back, but it is a snare, TRAP, which is reversed to give PART.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall apart is an idiom for breaking down or collapsing, physically or emotionally.

clue.text: Outing cut short in old part of Jerusalem

indicators.note: in tells us the shortened word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former or old
Sion is an old spelling of Zion, the hill in Jerusalem

indicators.note: short tells us to drop the last letter of the word for brusque

parts.note: curt means brusque, cut short in speech

explanation.surface: A day trip curtailed somewhere in the Old City of Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' reads as one phrase, but 'short' is a separate signal trimming the synonym; 'in' then places the result. SION is an old spelling of Zion.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion is a short pleasure trip, the same thing as an outing.

clue.text: Teacher using a couple of books in scripture lesson once

indicators.note: in places the article and the books inside the lesson's letters

parts.note: RI, Religious Instruction, was the old name for scripture lessons in British schools
B is an abbreviation for book, so two books give BB

explanation.surface: A teacher conducting an old-style scripture class with a couple of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and teacher of religious law; the word means 'my master'.

clue.text: Flog rubbish Henry imported

indicators.note: imported means brought inside, so the letter goes into the word for rubbish

parts.note: trash is rubbish
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A trader trying to sell junk brought in by someone called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' suggests selling, but here it means to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat with a whip or stick, which is to thrash.

clue.text: Jokes about an oriental language

indicators.note: about means the jokes wrap around the article

parts.note: japes are jokes or pranks
E for east, as oriental means eastern

explanation.surface: Humour involving an Asian language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oriental language' looks like a single definition, but 'oriental' only gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese is the language spoken in Japan.

clue.text: Very cool in the shade?

definitions.meaning: something in shadow cannot be seen

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is dated slang meaning fantastic; the second is a loose cryptic reading of being hidden in shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: dated slang for excellent, and literally unseen, as something in darkness is.

clue.text: Price not exorbitant, we're told, for pastry

indicators.note: we're told signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken

parts.note: a price that is not high is a fee low

explanation.surface: Pastry advertised as reasonably priced.
explanation.definitionFit: Filo is very thin, flaky pastry used in Greek and Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Recalled old record being played? Definitely not

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are taken in reverse

parts.note: EP, an extended-play record, is an old format
a record being played is on

explanation.surface: Asked whether an old record is being played again, someone flatly refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Nope is an emphatic informal way of saying no.

clue.text: Style of reporter heading out of country during short trip

indicators.note: during means the shortened country sits within the shortened trip
short means the trip loses its last letter

parts.note: a journey is a trip

indicators.note: heading out of means the country's first letter is dropped

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK

explanation.surface: A reporter's travel writing about a short trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: JOURNE (the trip cut short) is wrapped around ALES (Wales without its head).
explanation.definitionFit: Journalese is the clichéd, hackneyed writing style typical of newspapers.

clue.text: First of crimes in detective's largely well-trodden patch

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, so detective's gives DI's

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the shortened word
largely means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: trite means overused or well-trodden

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of crimes

explanation.surface: A detective's familiar beat, where crimes keep cropping up.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIT (trite, largely) takes C inside, after DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A district is an area or region, as is a patch, especially an officer's beat.

clue.text: Keen to do a turn with Italian singer

indicators.note: to do a turn means the word for crying is turned round

parts.note: to keen is to wail or weep
It is short for Italian, as in vermouth

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic Italian singer eager to perform a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like eager but is the verb to wail; 'singer' is crosswordese for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, or lapwing, is a bird, and birds are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Rabbit liver spread, right for eating

indicators.note: for eating means the spread takes the letter in

parts.note: pâté is a spread often made from liver

explanation.surface: Rabbit liver pâté, made correctly, ready to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like food but is the British slang verb to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly, which is to prate.

clue.text: So long! I'm off about start of Eton's new term

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go around the next piece
off means the letters are out of order, scrambled
start of picks out the first letter of the school's name

explanation.surface: A boy says goodbye as he leaves at the start of the new school term at Eton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' scrambles SOLONGIM, and that goes around E, the start of Eton's.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly coined word or expression, so a new term in language.

clue.text: Piano removed from leader's office for group's venue

indicators.note: removed from means the letter is taken out

parts.note: a presidency is the office of a leader
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A piano is cleared out of the boss's office to make room for a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A residency is a regular engagement for a band at one venue.

clue.text: Bridge partners always make derisory comments

parts.note: South and North are partners at bridge
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A pair of bridge players who constantly mock their opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To sneer is to make scornful, contemptuous remarks.

clue.text: Western stew containing semi-cold vegetable

indicators.note: containing means the scrambled letters hold the half word
stew means the letters are stirred and mixed up

parts.note: half of the word cold is CO

explanation.surface: A cowboy stew with half-cold corn in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western stew' reads as a dish, but 'stew' scrambles WESTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetcorn is maize grown to be eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Fellow's stretch limo, might one say?

parts.note: OS means outsize, so a stretch limo is an outsize vehicle
a limo is a car

explanation.surface: Someone says a man's long limousine is impressive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow's' is the definition plus 'is'; 'might one say?' admits the playful description of a stretch limo.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar is a man's first name, so it can stand for a fellow.

clue.text: Pinching pots, gent leaves the straight and narrow?

indicators.note: pinching means holding tight, so the gent grips the pots inside

parts.note: a toff is an upper-class gent
urns are pots

explanation.surface: A well-off man steals pots and goes to the bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' sounds like stealing but here means gripping. The definition is literal: a road that turns off leaves the straight road.
explanation.definitionFit: A road turns off when it branches away from a straight main route.

clue.text: Entertainment provided by Frasier every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means taking alternate letters of the sitcom title

explanation.surface: Light amusement offered by watching Frasier now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair, a funfair with rides and stalls, is a place of entertainment.

clue.text: Course includes bread and Irish cheese

indicators.note: includes means the word for course holds the other pieces

parts.note: a lane is a course, as in a running track
bread is slang for money, cash

explanation.surface: A meal course of bread and Irish cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire is a crumbly English cheese named after the county.

clue.text: A stretch of water in another country

parts.note: a broad is a lake in the Norfolk Broads, the East Anglian waterways

explanation.surface: A lake or channel somewhere overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means in or to a foreign land.

clue.text: Takes casual steps to get fish in Lake District location

parts.note: a person who walks leisurely ambles
the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A walker strolls to a spot in the Lakes to catch a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambleside is a town at the head of Windermere in the English Lake District.

clue.text: Opening of takeaway with ready-to-eat food

indicators.note: opening of picks out the first letter of takeaway

parts.note: fruit that is ready to eat is ripe

explanation.surface: A takeaway's launch, featuring ready-made meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is cow's stomach lining, eaten as food.

clue.text: Working to support Spanish clergyman

indicators.note: to support in a down clue means placed beneath, after the other piece

parts.note: a Minorcan comes from Minorca, a Spanish island
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Working to back a Spanish priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor canon is a clergyman serving a cathedral but not a member of its chapter.

clue.text: Cafes serving variety of pasta, but not seconds

indicators.note: variety of means a different arrangement of the letters

parts.note: bar means except, but not, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Restaurants offering assorted pasta dishes but no second helpings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas bars are Spanish-style cafés serving small snacks.

clue.text: One doing extra work on watch?

parts.note: over and on can both mean above
a timer is a watch or clock

explanation.surface: Someone working late while keeping an eye on the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is extra hours, and someone who works them is an overtimer.

clue.text: After party on the Champs Elysées we must appear hungry

indicators.note: after means the French pronoun follows the party

parts.note: a rave is a party
nous is French for we

explanation.surface: After a Paris party, people declare they are starving.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenous means very hungry, ready to eat anything.

clue.text: When does the weekend start, mate?

parts.note: the reply is at the close of Friday

explanation.surface: Someone asks a pal when the weekend begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is answered in a clipped way as Fri end, which also reads as a word for a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a pal or companion, and so a friend.

clue.text: Drug dealer caught in well-planned operation

indicators.note: caught in means the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A drug dealer arrested in a well-planned police raid.
explanation.definitionFit: A doper is one who gives or takes drugs, so a loose fit for a dealer.

clue.text: Report from Tory author

indicators.note: report means a spoken account, so it signals a word heard

parts.note: Tories are on the political right

explanation.surface: A news piece by a Conservative writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author' is a verb here, as in to author a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To author something is to compose it, and so to put it in writing.

clue.text: Place of learning? Yes, originally

indicators.note: originally means the opening letters of each of the earlier words

explanation.surface: A query whether somewhere was a school, answered yes, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: these polytechnics became universities in 1992, so they were originally places of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A poly, short for polytechnic, was a college of higher education in Britain.
